# STORYFORGE II ‚AI PIXEL-ART VISUAL OVERHAUL TO MATCH THE REFERENCE

## 0. Starting point
Work from the code in the project checkout as it is now. Earlier work that was never
merged (old case branches, anything under .devion/worktrees) is abandoned: do not read
it, merge it or copy from it. Where something is missing, build it fresh.
Already in place and to be kept: React shell, Phaser 3.90 host, data-driven scene
builder, content schema, asset manifest, game store, Story Panel, contribution dialog.
The art is placeholder: every asset is a tiny flat SVG. This goal replaces the look.

Reference image: game/docs/reference/storyforge-ui-reference.png. Open it before
planning and before judging. Section 2 describes it in words.

## 1. Hard constraints
- Phaser stays on 3.90.x. React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Radix, Zustand stay.
- Keep the Go API contracts and the contribution flow. No mock data in place of real calls.
- Scene content stays data-driven: no object, position or asset hardcoded in a scene class.
- All art is raster pixel art generated inside the repo from source data by a
  deterministic script. No downloaded art, no image services, no CDN links.
- One native scene resolution of 480x270, scaled by whole numbers only, nearest-neighbour.
- One shared palette of at most 48 colours, defined once and used by art and UI.
- Fonts are bundled through npm packages, not loaded from a URL.

## 2. Visual target
A cosy night-time bedroom in rich pixel art with a framed adventure-game interface.
- Mood: deep indigo and plum shadows, warm wood, brass and gold trim, parchment cream.
  Cool moonlight from the window against warm lamp light on the desk.
- Header bar, wood with brass corners: gold "STORYFORGE" logo, a plaque with the world
  name, a round pill with a status dot and the round id, the countdown, a gold primary
  button "+ SUGGEST WHAT HAPPENS NEXT", sound and settings icons.
- Game area, about three quarters of the width: striped wallpaper over wood wainscot,
  plank floor, window with curtains and a crescent moon, desk with an old computer,
  lamp and plant, wall poster, bookshelf with books and a globe, bed with a patterned
  blanket, door with light under it, rug, and the boy in a blue hoodie.
- Selected object: a name plate above it ("OLD BOOKSHELF") with its actions as small
  buttons beneath (INSPECT, SEARCH, PUSH) and a hand cursor.
- Right panel in the same frame style: chapter title, a parchment card with the
  speaker's portrait, name and line, the available choices as a list, a 3x2 inventory
  grid with item icons and names, and a short event log.

## 3. Deliverables
3.1 Art pipeline. Sprites are authored as palette-indexed pixel grids in source files.
    A script turns them into PNG sprite sheets and updates the manifest. The drawing
    code is pure functions, so tests can check size, frame count and palette use.
3.2 Room art. Layered PNGs for wall, wainscot, floor, window with night sky, and each
    piece of furniture and each object in section 2, with shading and outlines, drawn
    at native scale. Every placeholder SVG of the room is replaced and removed.
3.3 Character. The boy as a 32x48 sprite with idle (4 frames), walk (6) and interact
    (4) animations, plus a 32x32 portrait for the dialogue card.
3.4 Light and atmosphere. Moonlight shaft, lamp glow, light under the door, drifting
    dust and a soft vignette, built from scene content and placed on the effects layer.
3.5 Interface frame kit. Nine-slice frames for bar, panel, plaque, parchment card,
    inventory slot and buttons (normal, hover, pressed, disabled), a hand cursor, and
    design tokens for colour, spacing and type shared by every component.
3.6 Header rebuilt on the kit, showing live round id, status and countdown.
3.7 Story panel rebuilt on the kit: chapter title, dialogue card with portrait,
    choices, inventory grid with item icons, event log. It scrolls on its own.
3.8 Object interaction in the scene: hover highlight, name plate, action buttons
    anchored to the object, driven by the object's content definition.
3.9 Behaviour carried over from the last goal:
    - Game actions play the character's interact animation and scene changes fade.
    - A scene change to an empty or unknown scene is ignored.
    - Every interactive object can be reached and used by keyboard and screen reader,
      with labels from the same game state. The unused hotspot-over-image path is removed.
3.10 The game screen uses all of the above: no placeholder art or old styling remains.

## 4. Skills this work needs
Propose agents whose skills are the techniques below, written as reusable know-how:
- Pixel-art sprite authoring: silhouettes, outlines, shading with colour ramps, dithering.
- Limited-palette design: building ramps and keeping warm and cool light consistent.
- Sprite-sheet layout and frame animation timing.
- Pixel-perfect rendering: whole-number scaling, nearest-neighbour, device pixel ratio.
- Layered 2D lighting and particles in a scene engine.
- Nine-slice interface frames and state variants.
- Design tokens and component styling in a utility-CSS setup.
- Anchoring DOM overlays to objects in a canvas scene.
- Accessible alternatives for canvas content.
- Generating image files from data with deterministic, testable code.

## 5. Done when
- Every asset in the manifest is a generated PNG at its declared size using only the
  shared palette, and no placeholder SVG is referenced.
- The game screen shows the room, the boy, the lighting and the framed interface as
  section 2 describes, with the header, panel and object interaction working on real data.
- Section 3.9 behaviour works and is covered by unit tests.
- Layout holds from 1280x720 up, and the panel becomes a bottom drawer on narrow screens.

## 6. Out of scope
New rooms, new story content, backend changes, audio, deployment, repository clean-up.
